title: Finite Krein boundary corrections with GKN scope checks
summary: Explicit two- and four-trace right inverses preserve polynomial constraints; regular boundary-form dimensions and isotropy are checked separately from matrix rank.
conditions: Regular constant-coefficient expression c-D^2 on (-1,1), c>0.
Use the actual maximal/minimal domains and deficiency counts: (2,2) at order two, (4,4) at order four.
Sobolev approximation and continuous trace bounds must be supplied before inferring any graph-core or closure result.
For the divisible correction use an even integer L>=2 and the two polynomials x^L,x^(L+1).
scope: Boundary algebra for the current operator, not the unverified singular Legendre examples in arXiv1706.01539v1; rank alone does not certify GKN isotropy or density.
content: B on (x^L,x^(L+1)) is [[L,L],[-L,L]], determinant 2L^2. For residual (u,v), subtract (u-v)x^L/(2L)+(u+v)x^(L+1)/(2L). For T=(Bf,Bf''), the columns x^2,x^3,x^4,x^5 form [[2,2,4,4],[-2,2,-4,4],[0,0,24,40],[0,0,-24,40]], determinant15360. The skew boundary form is separately isotropic on the Krein square-domain trace subspace. L04 Proposition2.14 is an independence criterion in the boundary quotient; this residual matrix is a different object. Numerical rank or substituting arbitrary p_n for eigenfunction GKN data is insufficient.
